title: I made it! Google play approved my game!
author: OGZamasu
selftext:
I'm pretty happy today! Google Play approved my mobile game that I've been working on. I made this game using Claude Opus and Sonnet 5.5. I even made a trailer for it! 

  
I never imagined we would have such useful tools at our disposal to make projects like this. 

  
I would love to see some of your projects that you've shipped using Claude or Codex as well.

I heard Fable 5.5 is coming very soon too, and I cannot wait. I feel the creativity really flowing, and I see so many of you making things that inspire me. 

  
I think I want to try using Unreal for my next project. I saw that there was a new plugin for it released by Epic just recently. 

https://reddit.com/link/1x9mlwu/video/kaz6sh2bicwh1/player

If you'd like to check out my game, you can download it here.   


[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.zamasu.shardfall](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.zamasu.shardfall)

replies.author: OGZamasu
replies.body:
I just used claude. I actually packaged up a little handoff zip for my friend who also was making a game, and his trailer came out pretty good. If you'd like, I could send it over. I just used Sonnet 5.5 really, and told it it could use Opus subagents if it needed to.

This is the prompt that Sonnet gave it's subagent to make the trailer:  
`Make a trailer for SHARDFALL, the voxel-fantasy survivors-like in /Volumes/T9/Static Saints (player-facing name SHARDFALL, tagline "HOLD BACK THE BLIGHT"; repo/package still called static-saints on purpose). The user loved the trailer made for Sporefall: look at /Volumes/T9/sporefall-trailer (and the Sporefall project in /Volumes/T9/sporefall) first to see how it was produced, and reuse that approach and tooling wherever it fits. Done = finished, watchable trailer files in /Volumes/T9/Static Saints/artifacts/trailer/ : a 16:9 cut (1920x1080) and a 9:16 vertical cut (1080x1920, since the game is portrait-first and phone-first), roughly 45-75 seconds, H.264 mp4 with audio, plus a short README in that folder explaining how to re-render. Use REAL gameplay captured from the game itself (Playwright, headless Chromium; Playwright 1.63 is at /Volumes/T9/Gears/node_modules/playwright with browsers cached; ffmpeg is /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg). Show the hook (a star shattering, shards falling), the survivors loop (shard pickups, weapon draft, evolutions, the big hordes), the four stages and their bosses (Elderstone Colossus, Cinderwing, Yeti King, Blight Lord), heroes/pets/armor, and the daily/meta layer, ending on a clean title card with the SHARDFALL logo and a play call-to-action pointing at the website. The repo's scripts/ folder already has capture helpers (shots.ts, ui-shots.ts, walkthrough-video.ts, probe-game) worth reading. Music and sound: use the game's own procedural audio engine and/or generated audio, whatever the Sporefall trailer did; keep it punchy and mix it properly (no clipping). Constraints: do not edit the game's source under src/ (another session is concurrently adding an embed/arcade mode and framing headers to that repo, so keep your changes confined to artifacts/trailer/ and any new scripts you add). Capture from the repo's local dev build on a free port, NOT the live website (the live deploy is stale and still titled STATIC SAINTS). Do not deploy anything, do not commit or push, and never add GitHub Actions or hosted CI. If the trailer needs a copy line, keep any voice first-person singular or neutral (Zamasu is a studio of one), and never put the owner's personal name in it. When finished, report the output paths, duration, what footage/sections it contains, and anything you would improve with more time.`

If you want I can DM you a download to the handoff zip where it essentially made the whole thing with scripts.

replies.author: OGZamasu

I have 15 years of experience writing software and microservices. Really just let's me have a good idea of what choices I want to make for stuff. As long as you have a rough idea of the tech choices you want to make, or you take the time to research before you solidify your choices, you'll do great. 

Right now is a great time to get into it. It's like having a Jr Developer on my team. 

Cloudflare is really awesome too because they give so many free resources to us to use. Each domain name gets its own allowance of free resources on Cloudflare. Most things can be hosted on the free plan.

comments.body: Claude create all the assets and art? Can u explain the process?

replies.author: OGZamasu
replies.body: Yeah, everything is procedurally generated in Typescript. I started out explaining the concept, a mystical horde survival and dungeon game. I told it that I wanted to use WebGL and that I would have lots of enemies on screen. It put out a demo that, while it was ugly, it was a lot of fun. After I was satisfied it could handle all the stuff on screen,  Opus 5.5 and Sonnet came out. I told them I enjoyed the game and described the new art style I wanted to aim for. It really just all started with a basic web page where I would try to survive. Then I picked out a hand full of things I felt would be fun to add. I wanted it to have a sense of leveling up and collecting to help the player get further and encourage replaying. I added dungeons for that too. Once it was good enough for me to play on my phone, and I tested it for a hand full of hours,  I started the Google Play submission process, knowing it would take 3 weeks as this is my 2nd shipped game. I thought about what makes a game rewarding to play every day. I thought about what happens if you don't return every day. Added a daily reward streak with an ad to save your streak or get a 2nd free chest of the day. I didnt want ads to be intrusive or required. It's my first time adding ads to anything I made. During the 3 weeks I kept testing and sharing with other developers and friends. Now I guess I'm gonna keep playing every day or two and thinking of any ideas I wish the game had.

replies.author: Feisty-Ad-1805
replies.body: Wow thanks a lot for the explanation, but just one more important thing, if you used web technologies, how did u export your .APK ? O what process dis u follow?

replies.author: OGZamasu
replies.body:
Claude made me a custom Java WebView wrapper app. You could also use something like capacitor. It's basically the same but mine is super lightweight. 

I didn't want to do a PWA or a TWA because TestersCommunity had instructions to avoid doing that. It allows the game to be ran offline along with native android code for stuff like admob. Trying to do the same for iOS. 

I think the biggest reason I went this route was that a lot of my projects used three.js. I probably went thru about 50 projects before I started to decide what I really wanted to spend more time on and bring to production. 

My ADHD is a big factor here. And I was spending about 600 a month on subscriptions for a little bit, I had too many tokens to experiment with. I learned so much along the way.
